# Byron Donalds Watchdog File

**Subject:** Byron Donalds, Republican nominee for Governor of Florida, 2026
**Compiled:** October 23, 2026 for the On Point Politics watchdog database, onpointpolitics.us
**Data cutoff:** October 22, 2026. Next scheduled data drop: Florida Division of Elections filings due October 30, 2026
**Status conventions:** Every figure carries a date or as-of period. Rows marked provisional or contested are not yet confirmed by primary filings. The Yass to Kohelet link is contested and must not be stated as fact; see Part 1 section on Kohelet and Part 2 section on Claws Foundation.

## How this file is organized

- Part 1: first hop. Who funds Donalds, his committees, his own disclosures, Erika Donalds' Optima entities, and the Yass and Kohelet question.
- Part 2: second hop. What each funding bloc wants, what the governor controls, the decision calendar through 2028, and what changes for Floridians.
- Part 3: merged Ledger import table, 423 rows, both hops, with a Hop column.
- Part 4: raw research notes behind both reports, with inline source URLs, for verification and for extending the database.

## Entity index for the database

Core subject: Byron Donalds. Spouse: Erika Donalds. Committees: Friends of Byron Donalds PAC, FL DOE 89043; Byron Donalds for Governor; Byron Donalds for Congress, FEC C00733329; Proven Conservatives PAC, FEC C00755728 and C00894147; Byron Donalds Victory Fund, FEC C00760108. Treasurer for all: Bradley T. Crate, Red Curve Solutions, Beverly MA. Chair: Ryan Smith. Campaign manager: Chris Hudson.

Interest blocs used as tags: Billionaire megadonor; School choice and family; Gambling; Detention vendors; Utilities and energy; Utilities and data centers; Developers and construction; Insurance and tort; Crypto and finance; AI industry; Sugar and agriculture; Pro-Israel; Trump world; Enforcement and disclosure; Legislative leadership; Opponent context; Rival context.

Shared-lever office: Attorney General James Uthmeier, who shares donors with Donalds across gambling, detention and prediction markets.

---

# PART 1: FIRST HOP

# Billionaires, Bookmakers and Jailers Bankroll Donalds

Byron Donalds has raised nearly $149 million for governor as of October 20, 2026, and roughly nine tenths of it runs through one unlimited state committee, Friends of Byron Donalds PAC, whose largest checks come from Ken Griffin at $10 million, Jeff Yass at about $11 million counting his pass-through to Club for Growth Action Florida, the Seminole Tribe at $5.5 million, the GEO Group at $2.5 million to $3.5 million, and Richard Uihlein at $2 million, per the [Tampa Bay Times](https://kdhnews.com/news/politics/18-billionaires-have-funded-the-florida-governor-race-17-gave-to-donalds/article_f4a68240-1521-537e-b8cb-9006156ebc14.html) and [Florida Phoenix](https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/10/20/democratic-governors-association-investing-1-million-to-support-david-jolly/). Seventeen billionaires gave him $23.3 million, about two thirds of his money came from corporations, political committees and donors giving $10,000 or more, and 30 percent came from outside Florida. The donors cluster into eleven identifiable blocs, and in nearly every one the record contains a policy ask Donalds has already answered: he opposes a utility return cap after NextEra and Duke gave $1.5 million, he pledges to keep the 2023 tort reforms that insurers and Americans for Prosperity want, he sponsored the detention bills GEO lobbied for before GEO wrote seven-figure checks, and he and his wife Erika run a household whose reported wealth is almost entirely her for-profit charter management firms, which would sit under the Department of Education he would oversee. The one claim the user should not make is that Jeff Yass funded Israel's Kohelet Policy Forum: Haaretz reported it in 2021, but the New York Times, the Washington Post and Calcalist all reported that Yass never donated and that Arthur Dantchik was the dominant funder who withdrew in August 2023. The personal finance file is a pattern of under-disclosure corrected only after press reports: a Campaign Legal Center complaint over 108 unreported trades, four years of omitted liabilities amended in June 2026, a Federal Election Commission deadlock on a 2020 soft money chain, a rebuffed FEC demand to refund roughly $400,000, and a bitcoin purchase on the same day he signed a letter asking the IRS to loosen crypto tax rules. The next data drop is the October 30, 2026 Florida disclosure deadline, which will settle the late September and October gifts that are currently reported only by secondary outlets.

## Two state vehicles and a treasurer who also serves Trump

Donalds runs a capped candidate account, Byron Donalds for Governor, and the unlimited affiliated committee Friends of Byron Donalds PAC, Florida Division of Elections account 89043, chaired by campaign chief strategist Ryan Smith with treasurer Bradley T. Crate of Red Curve Solutions in Beverly, Massachusetts, per the [Division of Elections](https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/committees/ComDetail.asp?account=89043). Crate is also treasurer of every federal Donalds committee: Byron Donalds for Congress, FEC ID C00733329; the leadership PAC Proven Conservatives PAC, C00755728; a second leadership PAC, Proven Conservatives PAC Federal, registered December 19, 2024; and the Byron Donalds Victory Fund joint fundraising committee whose participants include the NRCC and the Republican Party of Florida, per [FEC committee records](https://www.fec.gov/data/committee/C00760108/). Red Curve is the compliance shop used by Trump's campaign and MAGA Inc., so the treasurer is the clearest documented vendor link to Trump world.

The scale of the state committee dwarfs anything in his federal history. His House committee raised **$3.25 million in 2020, $5.66 million in 2022 and $6.60 million in 2024**, per [FEC candidate pages](https://www.fec.gov/data/candidate/H2FL14186/?cycle=2024&election_full=true). The state PAC alone had taken in nearly $130.4 million through the October 3 to 9, 2026 reporting week, per the [Bradenton Journal](https://thebradentonjournal.substack.com/p/donations-from-neal-beruff-add-to), and combined totals reached **$134.4 million raised and $91.7 million spent by September 25**, per [CBS Miami](https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/byron-donalds-new-ads-florida-governor-race-david-jolly/). Through May 31, 2026 the split was $71.8 million to the PAC against $9.2 million to the candidate account across 35,292 donors, per [Floridian Press](https://floridianpress.com/2026/06/byron-donalds-adds-13-8-million-to-gubernatorial-war-chest-brings-total-to-over-81-million/). Because Florida allows unlimited gifts to a candidate's affiliated committee, most of what would be outside super PAC money in a federal race flows directly into Friends of Byron Donalds, which means federal-style independent expenditure reporting badly understates the picture. David Jolly, by comparison, had raised under $22 million by October 20, with Donald Sussman at $600,000 and Charles Wall at $525,000 as his largest donors, per [WUSF](https://wusf.org/text/politics-issues/2026-09-09/what-to-know-about-pacs-your-florida-breaks-it-down).

The rest of this report is organized as a money map: one section per interest bloc, each naming the donors, the amounts and dates the notes could document, what that bloc wants from Tallahassee, and what Donalds has done or pledged that aligns. Within each section, documented facts are separated from inference.

## Billionaire megadonors: Griffin, Yass, Uihlein, Peterffy, Wynn, DeVos

Documented. Ken Griffin of Citadel gave **$10 million** to the Donalds committee, reported July 24, 2026 and the largest single contribution in the race; Griffin also gave $2.5 million to Senator Ashley Moody, per the [Tampa Bay Times](https://www.tampabay.com/news/florida-politics/elections/2026/07/24/ken-griffin-byron-donalds-governor-donation-campaign-finance/). Jeff Yass of Susquehanna International Group gave **$5 million by March 31, 2025**, per [News4Jax](https://www.news4jax.com/news/local/2025/04/14/byron-donalds-secures-6-million-from-influential-gop-donors-in-early-fundraising-for-florida-governors-race/), reaching **$7.5 million** by mid 2026, per [Miami New Times](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/news/the-tiktok-billionaire-bankrolling-byron-donalds-40558946/), plus **$3.5 million to Club for Growth Action Florida, which in turn gave Friends of Byron Donalds $3.75 million**, for a total WUSF puts at $11 million, per [WUSF](https://wusf.org/text/politics-issues/2026-09-09/what-to-know-about-pacs-your-florida-breaks-it-down). Richard Uihlein of Uline gave $1 million by March 31, 2025 and a second $1 million on June 6, 2025, per [Florida Politics](https://floridapolitics.com/archives/745791-byron-donalds-adds-to-haul-for-governors-race-bringing-total-to-22m/). Thomas Peterffy of Interactive Brokers gave $1.2 million, Steve Wynn gave $1 million in the first quarter of 2026, and the DeVos family gave about $1 million combined, per [Miami New Times](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/news/the-tiktok-billionaire-bankrolling-byron-donalds-40558946/), the [Highlands News-Sun](https://www.midfloridanewspapers.com/highlands_news-sun/news/donalds-dominates-fundraising-in-governor-race/article_70925d94-73c0-4f61-9737-e3805c0a1d70.html) and the [Tampa Bay Times](https://kdhnews.com/news/politics/18-billionaires-have-funded-the-florida-governor-race-17-gave-to-donalds/article_f4a68240-1521-537e-b8cb-9006156ebc14.html). Eric Schmidt, the former Google chief executive, gave $500,000 in the October 3 to 9 week, per the [Bradenton Journal](https://thebradentonjournal.substack.com/p/donations-from-neal-beruff-add-to). Early 2025 donors also included Clive Fields at $500,000 and Deborah Magowan at $150,000, per [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/ron-desantis-florida-lobbyists-rep-byron-donalds-governor-rcna196996).

Yass's relationship with Donalds predates the governor race but ran through intermediaries. Club for Growth Action, funded in the 2020 cycle by Uihlein at $26.5 million and Yass at $1.7 million, per [FactCheck.org](https://www.factcheck.org/2020/01/club-for-growth-action-5), spent **about $2.5 million** in the 2020 FL-19 primary that Donalds won by 777 votes, per [Club for Growth](https://www.clubforgrowth.org/cfg-pac-endorses-rep-byron-donalds-in-fl-gov-race/) and [ProPublica](https://projects.propublica.org/itemizer/races/2020/states/fl/house/19). Protect Freedom PAC, roughly 80 to 95 percent funded by Yass per the [Kentucky Lantern](https://kentuckylantern.com/2024/04/11/billionaire-tiktok-investor-charter-school-advocate-puts-8-million-into-paul-affiliated-pac/), was the only outside group active for Donalds in all three House cycles, at about $80,000 in 2020, $30,000 in 2022 and $10,000 in 2024, per ProPublica independent expenditure pages. No direct Yass check to any federal Donalds committee was found in any source, and the federal limit would cap it at $3,300 per election. Club for Growth PAC endorsed Donalds for governor on March 11, 2025, citing his 100 percent lifetime rating, per [Club for Growth](https://www.clubforgrowth.org/cfg-pac-endorses-rep-byron-donalds-in-fl-gov-race/). Yass gave $16 million to MAGA Inc. in the first half of 2025 and is reported at $110 million for the 2026 GOP cycle, per [Spectrum News](https://spectrumlocalnews.com/us/snplus/politics/2026/10/16/midterm-elections-top-50-donors-decision-2026).

What this bloc wants. Yass has said school choice is his main political motivation and a Susquehanna spokesperson called Donalds "a school choice warrior," per [Miami New Times](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/news/the-billionaire-trying-to-reinvent-florida-schools-has-a-7-5-million-bet-on-byron-donalds-40565603/). Club for Growth's agenda is tax cuts, "education freedom" and limited government. Griffin's firm helped push an expansion of the charter co-location program Donalds co-sponsored, per [Florida Trib](https://flaglerlive.com/gospel-of-school-choice/). Uihlein, Yass and Griffin were all DeSantis donors who migrated to Donalds before DeSantis endorsed him on September 1, 2026, per [News4Jax](https://gmg-wjxt-prod.cdn.arcpublishing.com/news/local/2025/04/14/byron-donalds-secures-6-million-from-influential-gop-donors-in-early-fundraising-for-florida-governors-race) and the [Tampa Bay Times](https://www.aol.com/articles/billionaire-ken-griffin-pours-money-192303000.html).

What Donalds has done. He supports Amendment 3 and full elimination of homestead property taxes through the 2027 Tax and Budget Reform Commission, per [WLRN](https://www.wlrn.org/government-politics/2026-09-01/byron-donalds-doubles-down-on-cutting-or-even-eliminating-property-taxes-if-elected). His education plan expands vouchers with a heavy private sector role. A counterexample matters here: Donalds voted Yea on the March 13, 2024 TikTok divestiture bill, Roll Call 86, against the interest of Yass's ByteDance stake, per the [House Clerk](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/202486), and Yass's first $5 million arrived after that vote. Any claim that Yass money bought a TikTok position is contradicted by the record.

Inference. The split of Yass's $7.5 million is most likely $5 million in March 2025 and $2.5 million in the first quarter of 2026, and Florida Trib reports the latest $2.5 million came three days after a March 2026 Doral education event where Erika Donalds spoke, per [Florida Trib](https://floridatrib.org/2026/07/30/what-byron-and-erika-donalds-gospel-of-school-choice-could-mean-for-florida/). The exact dates are not confirmed from primary records.

## The Kohelet question: what can be said accurately

The user should treat this point as a landmine and state it precisely. Kohelet Policy Forum, founded in January 2012 by Moshe Koppel, produced the policy papers behind Israel's 2023 judicial overhaul and reportedly wrote the legislation submitted by Yariv Levin and Simcha Rothman, per [PBS and AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/an-american-billionaire-says-hell-stop-funding-the-think-tank-behind-israels-controversial-judicial-overhaul) and [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kohelet_Policy_Forum). In March 2021 Haaretz reported that both Jeff Yass and his Susquehanna co-founder Arthur Dantchik were behind a large portion of Kohelet's donations through opaque American vehicles, and The Intercept repeated that framing in February 2023 without amounts, per [The Intercept](https://theintercept.com/2023/02/16/israel-jeff-yass-kohelet). That is the alleged version.

The better-sourced version is different. Calcalist reported on August 4, 2023, citing sources close to Dantchik, that **Yass "never donated" to Kohelet**, and JTA wrote that this "confirms New York Times and Washington Post reporting and contradicts the 2021 Haaretz investigation," per [Calcalist](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/hkora4ci3) and [JTA](https://www.jta.org/2023/08/04/israel/wall-street-billionaire-ends-funding-for-think-tank-behind-netanyahus-judicial-overhaul-plan). The Washington Post's March 2023 source said Dantchik was not the sole funder but that Yass never gave, per [InfluenceWatch](https://www.influencewatch.org/person/jeffrey-yass/). Dantchik's giving is confirmed by his own statement that day: "I stopped donating to think tanks in Israel, including the Kohelet Policy Forum." A Shomrim investigation traced about $12 million in 2021 from Dantchik's Claws Foundation through Silver Valley Research Foundation to the Central Fund of Israel, which was Kohelet's sole listed donor that year, per [Shomrim](https://www.shomrim.news/eng/danchik-kohelet). Calcalist's reporting put Dantchik at roughly 93 percent of Kohelet's budget, per [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kohelet_Policy_Forum). After the withdrawal, Kohelet cut about half its staff in April 2024 and its donations fell from 30 million shekels in 2022 to 13.6 million in 2024, per [Israel Hayom](https://www.israelhayom.com/2024/04/02/kohelet-policy-forum-scales-down-activity-due-to-funding-crunch/) and [Shomrim](https://www.shomrim.news/eng/funding-crisis-forces-kohelet-to-cut-salaries-research-and-support-for-other-groups).

The defensible public formulation is: Donalds' largest donor, Jeff Yass, was named by Haaretz in 2021 as a Kohelet funder alongside his business partner Arthur Dantchik; later reporting by the New York Times, Washington Post and Calcalist found Yass never donated, while Dantchik, who was the dominant funder, publicly stopped giving in August 2023. No filing shows a Yass or Susquehanna Foundation grant to American Friends of Kohelet, the Central Fund of Israel or Silver Valley. Yass does have documented indirect ties to pro-Israel giving: the Guardian found the Claws Foundation, where he served as a director, gave $16 million to pro-Israel and anti-Muslim groups, per the [Daily Beast summary](https://blogs.thedailybeast.com/gop-megadonor-jeff-yass-poured-dollar16m-into-anti-muslim-groups-report). That is a different claim from funding Kohelet and should not be blended with it.

## School choice and the Donalds family businesses

Documented. The school choice bloc is the one where donor interest, candidate policy and household income converge. Yass's $7.5 million and Griffin's $10 million both come from avowed school choice backers, Erika Donalds met the Yasses after OptimaEd was a 2023 Yass Prize semifinalist, and Donalds co-sponsored the 2017 Schools of Hope law and the charter co-location law and chaired the Florida House PreK-12 Quality Subcommittee, per [Miami New Times](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/news/the-billionaire-trying-to-reinvent-florida-schools-has-a-7-5-million-bet-on-byron-donalds-40565603/) and the [Miami Herald](https://www.aol.com/articles/byron-donalds-runs-governor-wife-150251717.html). AFP Action, which endorsed him March 4, 2026, credits him with the legislation that created Florida's Hope Scholarship, per [AFP Action](https://afpaction.com/afp-action-endorses-byron-donalds-for-governor/). Turning Point Action endorsed him January 13, 2026 citing school choice and parental rights. Charles "Chip" Cordes, co-founder of Summit Construction, the firm that built the Optima schools, gave $8,400 to Donalds' House campaign in 2020, matched by his wife, plus $2,000 in 2021, per [Florida Bulldog](https://www.floridabulldog.org/2026/01/charter-business-owned-rep-donalds-wife-cut-side-deals-construction-firm-suit-says/).

What this bloc wants. Florida's universal voucher program costs about $4.5 billion a year for more than 500,000 students at roughly $8,000 each, and the Florida Education Association sued over it in May 2026, per [Florida Trib](https://floridatrib.org/2026/07/30/what-byron-and-erika-donalds-gospel-of-school-choice-could-mean-for-florida/). The ask is to protect and expand that program and to open it further to private operators and ed-tech vendors.

What Donalds has pledged. His plan puts parents "at the head of the table," replaces A to F school grades and annual testing with individualized learning plans, and treats parents as consumers and schools as competitors with a heavy AI and ed-tech role. Erika Donalds said in October 2026 that vouchers should be funded from the same pot as public and charter schools, per [WUSF](https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-10-19/erika-donalds-weighs-in-on-immigration-school-vouchers-state-power-over-local-governments), and said in March 2026 that "profit is not going to be a bad word when it comes to the education industry." Donalds' response is that "no donor has asked me to pursue school choice as governor because they don't have to." The Optima money flows that make this a conflict question are laid out in their own section below.

Inference. This is the bloc where the governor's office has the most direct levers: the Department of Education, the State Board of Education and the voucher administration all sit under the executive. No source documents a specific Donalds vote that benefited Optima, and Florida Bulldog says the same, but the structural overlap between the household's income and the office's authority is unlike any other bloc here.

## Gambling and prediction markets: more than $6 million ahead of a compact fight

Documented. The Seminole Tribe of Florida gave $1 million in August 2025, $1 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, $3 million cumulative by July 2026, another $1 million in August 2026, and **$5.5 million through September 18, 2026**, per [Florida Politics](https://floridapolitics.com/archives/753415-seminole-tribe-antes-up-with-byron-donalds/), [News4Jax](https://www.news4jax.com/news/politics/2026/01/15/rep-byron-donalds-continues-to-hold-wide-fundraising-advantage-in-floridas-race-for-governor-here-are-his-top-donors/) and [Bonus.com](https://www.bonus.com/news/gaming-money-flows-into-florida-governor-race-with-seminole-tribe-draftkings-and-fanduel-b/). FanDuel gave most of $581,000, DK Crown Holdings of DraftKings most of $525,000, the Sports Betting Alliance $250,000, Caesars $245,000, Robinhood $200,000, PrizePicks $100,000, the Poarch Band of Creek Indians $100,000 and Kalshi $75,000 through July 2026, per [Gambling Insider](https://www.gamblinginsider.com/news/185823/gambling-prediction-markets-florida-elections-byron-donalds) and [CardPlayer](https://www.cardplayer.com/poker-news/1735617-florida-campaign-donations-signal-possible-gaming-expansion). Steve Wynn gave $1 million. Gambling Insider totals the bloc at more than $6 million, and the Tampa Bay Times puts gaming at roughly 10 percent of his large-dollar money. Yass himself is described as a Kalshi investor.

What this bloc wants. The 2021 compact's exclusivity delivers about $1 billion a year to the state. Kalshi, Polymarket, FanDuel Predicts and DraftKings Predictions operate under CFTC oversight outside the compact, DeSantis said in February 2026 that a prediction market could conflict with the compact, and the Tribe wants online casino gaming, per [WOKV](https://www.wokv.com/news/local/could-prediction-market-offerings-put-floridas-gaming-compact-with-seminole-tribe-risk/N32U5WRRGJE4XLDEW4EILHUFSY/). The Tribe and the sportsbooks are on opposite sides of that fight and both are funding him.

What Donalds has done. He has taken no public position on prediction markets or the compact. Kalshi, a donor, ran a market showing him above 95 percent to win the primary, which he promoted on social media, per [Miami New Times](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/news/the-tiktok-billionaire-bankrolling-byron-donalds-40558946/).

Inference. Both sides buying access before a 2027 compact fight is the most plausible reading. The Tribe's August 2025 $1 million was described by Florida Politics as possibly hedging against a Casey DeSantis or Collins run, which suggests the Tribe is paying for a seat regardless of nominee rather than for a specific promise.

## Detention and immigration vendors owed $417 million

Documented. The GEO Group, the Boca Raton detention contractor, gave $500,000 by January 2026, $1.5 million across two gifts by July 2026, **$2.5 million by September 30, 2026**, and a further $1 million in the October 3 to 9 week, per [News4Jax](https://www.news4jax.com/news/politics/2026/01/15/rep-byron-donalds-continues-to-hold-wide-fundraising-advantage-in-floridas-race-for-governor-here-are-his-top-donors/), [WUSF](https://wusf.org/text/politics-issues/2026-09-30/immigration-detention-money-flows-florida-governors-race) and the [Bradenton Journal](https://thebradentonjournal.substack.com/p/donations-from-neal-beruff-add-to). GEO's PAC was already a $5,000 House donor in 2020 and gave $2,500 twice to the Victory Fund, per [ProPublica](https://projects.propublica.org/itemizer/committee/C00760108/2024/pac-donations). CDR entities and Carlos Duart gave more than $620,000, Access Restoration Services, parent of IRG, more than $100,000, Lemoine $59,000 and Critical Response Strategies $10,000, per [WUSF](https://wusf.org/text/politics-issues/2026-09-30/immigration-detention-money-flows-florida-governors-race). None gave to Jolly.

What this bloc wants. The Florida Division of Emergency Management owed more than $417 million on 592 unpaid Operation Vigil Sentry invoices: GEO's joint venture nearly $40 million, IRG more than $68 million, CDR more than $40 million, Lemoine $27.3 million and Critical Response more than $35 million, per WUSF. Separately, GEO spent $340,000 and $350,000 in the second half of 2024 lobbying for two Donalds bills, the Secure the Border Act he co-sponsored and the Reshape Alternatives to Detention Act he sponsored, and nearly $2 million lobbying overall that year.

What Donalds has pledged. He calls Alligator Alcatraz "mission accomplished," will pursue full federal reimbursement, and will remove local officials who create sanctuaries, suspend state attorneys, require E-Verify for all businesses and withhold grants under a "Zero Tolerance, Zero Dollars" plan, per [Florida Phoenix](https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/08/12/byron-donalds-says-hell-remove-local-officials-who-indulge-in-sanctuary-policies/) and [WFLX](https://www.wflx.com/2026/06/10/byron-donalds-calls-florida-immigration-crackdown-mission-accomplished-seeks-federal-repayment/).

Inference. WUSF is explicit that its reporting "does not establish whether donations were linked to contract decisions or payments." The sequence that stands out is GEO lobbying on his own bills in 2024, then giving seven figures in 2025 and 2026 while owed money by the state he seeks to run. That is the clearest "act, then money" sequence in the file. The next governor signs off on paying those invoices.

## Utilities, energy and data centers: $1.79 million career and a rejected rate cap

Documented. NextEra Energy, parent of FPL, gave $500,000 by January 2026 and $1 million by July 2026; Duke Energy $500,000; a TECO-associated company $125,000 in August 2026, per [News4Jax](https://www.news4jax.com/news/politics/2026/01/15/rep-byron-donalds-continues-to-hold-wide-fundraising-advantage-in-floridas-race-for-governor-here-are-his-top-donors/), [VoteWater](https://votewater.org/dirty-money-talks-what-does-it-say-about-byron-donalds/) and the [Miami Times](https://www.miamitimesonline.com/news/florida/daniel-perez-political-committees-give-1m-boost-to-byron-donalds-campaign-for-governor/article_8eab53e4-a074-412b-80fa-c2d4cc22cd7d.html). The CLEO Institute counts $1.79 million from Florida's major utilities across his career, second only to Wilton Simpson, per [Florida Phoenix](https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/donalds-and-jolly-bicker-over-response-utility-profitability). NextEra's PAC has given to his House committee every cycle, including $12,000 in 2026, per [FundVoter](https://fundvoter.org/politicians/byron-donalds). ## Erika Donalds' Optima entities and the conflict a governor cannot recuse from

The structure. Erika Donalds co-formed the nonprofit Optima Foundation in late 2017, renamed Education Freedom Foundation in March 2025, and then shifted the management business into two for-profit firms she owns through Onesto LLC, an anonymous Delaware entity formed in 2018 of which she is sole member: OptimaEd, formed 2020, 81 percent hers and converted to a C corporation in November 2025, and Optima Management Services, formed 2022 with her as founder and sole manager, per [Florida Bulldog](https://www.floridabulldog.org/2025/06/firms-belonging-to-rep-donalds-wife-grabbed-millions-in-charter-school-contracts/). A new entity, Dewalt Impact Group LLC of Lewes, Delaware, appears for the first time in the 2025 disclosure with business income of $100,001 to $1 million, while the Optima Management Services valuation fell from $1 million to $5 million down to $250,001 to $500,000, per the [2025 annual report](https://disclosures-clerk.house.gov/public_disc/financial-pdfs/2025/10075306.pdf). No reporting on Dewalt was found. She leads education policy at the America First Policy Institute, sits on a DeSantis-appointed FGCU trustee seat, and was a Heritage Foundation visiting fellow.

The dollar flows. Auditor filings show the Foundation received management fees of **$4,303,822 from Treasure Coast Classical, $8,424,572 from Naples Classical and $2,398,221 from Jacksonville Classical**, roughly $15.1 million; Optima-run schools paid Educator Solutions, a payroll firm founded by state Representative John Snyder that paid Erika more than $500,000 in salary, $6,930,584 in 2020 to 2022; the two for-profits took in **$5,843,969 in 2023 alone**; Naples Classical's 12 percent fee rose from $1.24 million to the Foundation in 2021 to 2022 to $1.56 million to Optima Management Services in 2023 to 2024; and the virtual Optima Classical Academy paid OptimaEd $1,085,266 in 2023 and $2.1 million in 2024, nearly **89 percent of the $3,588,660 in government funds** it received, per [Florida Bulldog](https://www.floridabulldog.org/2025/06/firms-belonging-to-rep-donalds-wife-grabbed-millions-in-charter-school-contracts/). CBS News found that between 2020 and 2023 the schools spent roughly 30 percent of their government funding, about **$35 million**, on outside firms tied to Erika, and a University of Miami charter expert found students at the four opened schools performed below average in math and reading, per [CBS via Ravitch](https://dianeravitch.net/2025/12/04/florida-wife-of-gop-gubernatorial-candidate-builds-a-for-profit-charter-school-empire). Summit Construction Management won $14.4 million, $20 million, $1 million and $11 million in building contracts for the schools, per [Florida Bulldog](https://www.floridabulldog.org/2026/01/charter-business-owned-rep-donalds-wife-cut-side-deals-construction-firm-suit-says/). The flows overlap and are not additive, but they are consistent with the CBS figure.

The breakups and lawsuits. Treasure Coast Classical terminated its Foundation contract December 31, 2023 and both Jacksonville academies ended ties in 2023 citing auditor deficiencies in debts, textbooks, revenues and vendor invoices. All four opened schools have cut ties. Treasure Coast Classical sued in late 2024, alleging Optima subcontracted all its employees to OptimaEd over a board veto, steered no-bid contracts to Summit, paid a $127,487.98 Summit invoice without authorization and failed to disclose that Summit-related entities had invested in Optima-related entities; a Martin County judge dismissed on venue grounds in May 2025 and the school appealed, per [Florida Bulldog](https://www.floridabulldog.org/2026/01/charter-business-owned-rep-donalds-wife-cut-side-deals-construction-firm-suit-says/). The Fort Myers campus that broke ground in 2023 never opened and was transferred to another operator in October 2025, which James Fishback used as a primary press event, per [Fox 4](https://www.fox4now.com/news/local-news/abandoned-fort-myers-charter-school-becomes-flashpoint-in-florida-governor-race). Paul Renner proposed a ban on first-time government contracts to officials and spouses and three-day trade disclosure in direct response, and Jay Collins' April 2026 opposition document led with the $35 million figure.

The conflict question. Erika says she does no business with the state of Florida and that there is "no conflict," and the campaign calls her work a longstanding career, per [Florida Trib](https://floridatrib.org/2026/07/30/what-byron-and-erika-donalds-gospel-of-school-choice-could-mean-for-florida/). The accurate framing is narrower than "state contracts" and more structural: her firms are paid by charter schools and a virtual academy whose revenue is state per-pupil funding and taxpayer scholarships, her Education Freedom Foundation sells consulting to charter founders in ESA states, and she publicly advocates funding vouchers from the same pot as public schools. No source quantified ESA dollars flowing to OptimaEd beyond the virtual charter's $3.59 million, and no ethics complaint or investigation specifically about her contracts was found, so the defensible claim is a structural conflict and a documented history of under-disclosure, not a documented quid pro quo.

The money map points to four interests with both the dollars and a live decision in front of the next governor: the gambling industry on both sides of a prediction market and compact fight he has not taken a position on; the detention vendors owed $417 million whose invoices he would approve; utilities and data center builders who need the PSC and siting law he has already promised not to tighten; and the school choice ecosystem that pays his household. Insurers and developers already have most of what they want and are paying to keep it. The billionaires at the top, Griffin, Yass, Uihlein and Peterffy, are buying a low-tax, school choice governor in the largest state they can, and his property tax elimination pledge is the clearest delivery on that. What the record does not show is a vote-for-check exchange on any single item, and Donalds' TikTok votes against Yass's core financial interest are the strongest evidence that he is not simply transactional.

The two vulnerabilities an opponent or a reporter can press without overstating are the disclosure pattern and the household conflict. Four years of inaccurate forms, a two-year PTR blackout, a 3 to 3 FEC deadlock and a rebuffed refund demand are documented and sourced. The Optima flows are documented to the dollar. The Kohelet claim is not, and using it would hand the campaign an easy rebuttal. The October 30 filing will tell whether the DeVos, Florida Crystals and Disney gifts reported secondhand are real and whether GEO's October $1 million lands as reported.

Byron Donalds' $149 million campaign is best understood not as a donor list but as a queue of decisions that will land on the governor's desk between January 2027 and the end of 2028, and the money sorts cleanly by which decision each donor needs. Behind those four stand the billionaires who fund the whole structure, Griffin and Yass above all, who want a low-tax, pro-business, school choice state and whose Florida asks are mostly preservation rather than change. Donalds has stated positions that satisfy the utilities, insurers, developers, AI investors and voucher operators, and has stayed silent on the one fight where his donors oppose each other, the Seminole compact versus prediction markets. What ordinary Floridians would experience is higher electric bills with no return cap, continued voucher expansion without audit controls, a detention program that keeps drawing general revenue, a property tax shift that costs local governments an estimated $12 billion a year with service cuts or fees to fill it, and a continued exodus from Citizens into pricier private policies. David Jolly's stated program reverses most of that: a return on equity cap at the national average, a data center moratorium, means-tested vouchers, an end to the 287g county mandate, Medicaid expansion and a state catastrophe wind fund.

## Gambling and prediction markets: the Tribe has already fired, and the governor must pick a side

Documented. The 2021 compact runs through July 31, 2051 and grants the Seminole Tribe exclusivity over slots, craps, roulette, banked card games, fantasy contests and statewide mobile sports betting through a hub-and-spoke server model, with the state guaranteed at least $2.5 billion over the first five years, per the [Florida Senate summary](https://www.flsenate.gov/PublishedContent/Offices/2020-2022/President/Documents/Summaryof2021Compact.pdf). The state's revenue estimators recorded **$817.3 million in revenue share in FY 2024 to 2025**, forecast **$903.3 million for FY 2025 to 2026**, and project more than $1 billion a year from FY 2028 to 2029, roughly $6.1 billion over the forecast period, per the [EDR Indian Gaming conference of Aug 4, 2025](https://edr.state.fl.us/Content/conferences/Indian-gaming/archives/250804IndianGaming.pdf). The compact's only built-in reopener was a 36-month good-faith negotiation window on online casino gaming, which closed in late 2024 without an amendment, per the same Senate summary. The governor executes compacts and must cooperate in seeking Interior approval, and compacts take effect only after legislative ratification, per [Fla. Stat. 285.710](https://codes.findlaw.com/fl/title-xix-public-business/fl-st-sect-285-710/). The governor also appoints all five members of the Florida Gaming Control Commission, subject to Senate confirmation, for four-year terms, and is barred from soliciting recommendations from anyone tied to a tribe's gaming operation, per [Fla. Stat. 16.71](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/16.71).

On October 8, 2026 the Tribe filed a 72-page complaint in Broward Circuit Court against DraftKings, CEO Jason Robins and GUS III LLC, the operator of DraftKings Predictions, seeking an injunction and disgorgement of all Florida revenue and a civil racketeering finding against Robins personally; the complaint alleges that on August 28, 2026 DraftKings replaced American odds with cent prices for Florida users and that "DraftKings changed the label on the price. It did not change the price, the product, or the transaction," per [Legal Sports Report](https://www.legalsportsreport.com/281066/draftkings-sued-by-seminole-tribe-over-sports-predictions-in-florida/). The same complaint alleges DraftKings secretly financed the West Flagler challenge and funded Protect the Constitution LLC, whose Amendment 3 suit Judge Jonathan Sjostrom dismissed for lack of standing on November 6, 2025 and which DraftKings joined as sole member on September 17, 2026; Attorney General James Uthmeier's office had urged dismissal in June 2025, per [CasinoBeats](https://casinobeats.com/2025/11/06/florida-judge-dismisses-protect-the-constitution-lawsuit-seminole-sports-betting/) and Legal Sports Report. Kalshi remains legal and available in Florida as of October 2026 with no state action against it, and HB 189, which would have made non-compact online wagering a third-degree felony, did not pass, per [Covers](https://www.covers.com/betting/prediction-sites/usa/florida-kalshi). Florida is one of six states that did not sign the attorneys general letter asserting state control over gambling, and Uthmeier "has taken a passive approach on prediction markets but has defended the tribe's compact," per [The Lines](https://www.thelines.com/legal-betting/seminole-tribe-spending-to-protect-florida-gambling-interests/). DeSantis raised the question publicly in February 2026, asking on CNBC whether "something like Kalshi" clashes with Florida law, per [Sportsbook Review](https://www.sportsbookreview.com/news/florida-governor-desantis-questions-kalshi-feb-25-2026/). The national map tightened in the fall: the Sixth Circuit held on September 25, 2026 that Kalshi had not shown its sports contracts are swaps under exclusive CFTC jurisdiction, the Ninth Circuit found two California tribes likely to succeed on IGRA claims, and 39 state attorneys general plus 130 tribes urged the Supreme Court to hear New Jersey's petition, per [Pillsbury](https://www.pillsburylaw.com/en/news-and-insights/indian-gaming-prediction-markets-scotus.html) and [CDC Gaming](https://cdcgaming.com/brief/tribe-39-state-attorneys-general-latest-to-ask-supreme-court-to-hear-prediction-markets-case/).

The Tribe's giving tracks every office that touches the compact: **$5.5 million to Friends of Byron Donalds, $1 million to Wilton Simpson, $750,000 to Senator Jim Boyd, $750,000 to the Republican Party of Florida, $200,000 to the Florida Democratic Party, $50,000 to Uthmeier and $50,000 to Charlie Crist's St. Petersburg mayoral run**, with nothing to Jolly, per [CardPlayer](https://www.cardplayer.com/?p=1735617), The Lines and [WLRN](https://www.wlrn.org/government-politics/2026-10-02/despite-detention-center-lawsuit-the-miccosukee-tribe-donated-to-supporters-of-alligator-alcatraz). Kalshi has given more than $400,000 in Florida, mostly to Republicans, including $50,000 to Uthmeier's committee and $150,000 to legislative leadership funds, per a [Gary Fineout post](https://x.com/fineout/status/2112529622047105389) whose body could not be read. The Poarch Band, which owns the Gretna track, a Pensacola card room and the Magic City Casino permit, gave $555,000 statewide, per [Gambling Insider](https://www.gamblinginsider.com/news/185823/gambling-prediction-markets-florida-elections-byron-donalds). Hard Rock CEO Jim Allen has said since 2024 that the Tribe would need to reopen talks on online casino gaming and that Hard Rock has "never" ruled out working with Caesars, BetMGM, DraftKings and FanDuel, per [Legal Sports Report](https://www.legalsportsreport.com/?p=178605). Donalds has said nothing on the compact, iGaming, prediction markets or the DraftKings suit in any source found; his adviser Danielle Alvarez says he "answers to no one but the people of Florida," per CardPlayer.

Inference. The money from both sides is a purchase of a seat at a renegotiation only the governor can convene. The most concrete Seminole ask is a compact amendment adding online casino gaming, which would need legislative ratification and would draw an Amendment 3 challenge; the most concrete prediction market ask is that Florida keep doing nothing. Because the Tribe has now sued privately, a Governor Donalds can preserve the status quo for a while by letting the Broward court and the Supreme Court decide, but the FGCC appointments and the AG's amicus choices are decisions he cannot defer forever. The 2010 compact precedent shows the cost of guessing wrong: when the state let pari-mutuels run designated player games, the Tribe stopped sharing banked game revenue and parked $19.5 million a month in a reserve the state could not touch, which Florida TaxWatch estimated at nearly $250 million lost, per [Florida TaxWatch](https://www.floridataxwatch.org/lack-of-a-seminole-gaming-compact-proving-very-costly-to-florida/). A governor who sides with prediction markets risks a similar withholding against a payment stream now near $900 million a year.

What changes for Floridians. If the compact is reopened for online casino gaming, Floridians get legal iGaming on their phones, the state gets a larger revenue share, and the pari-mutuels and commercial books get skins if the Tribe agrees. If the state does nothing, prediction markets keep operating at 18 plus with no Florida consumer protections, and the Tribe litigates alone. Either way, the $900 million payment that funds general revenue is the thing at risk, and that money is spread across every state program.

What Jolly would do instead. No Jolly gambling policy was found beyond attacking the donations; the Tribe gave him nothing, which suggests it does not expect him to reopen the compact on its terms.

The PSC unanimously approved FPL's settlement on November 20, 2025, described as a roughly $7 billion rate increase and the largest in state history, and the fight moved to the Florida Supreme Court over 2026 to 2027 rates, per [Florida Phoenix](https://floridaphoenix.com/2025/11/20/psc-approves-contentious-7-billion-rate-hike-for-florida-power-light-customers/), [E&E News](https://www.eenews.net/articles/psc-unanimously-approves-florida-power-light-rate-hike-settlement/) and [CBS Miami](https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/florida-fpl-energy-bill-new-rates-2026-2027/). DeSantis reappointed commissioners Gary Clark and Gabriella Passidomo-Smith in 2026, per the [governor's office](https://www.flgov.com/eog/news/press/2026/governor-ron-desantis-announced-reappointment-two-florida-public-service-commission); the governor picks from a list screened by the PSC Nominating Council, a joint legislative committee, per the [Florida Legislature](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/cgi-bin/View_Page.pl?File=index.cfm&Directory=committees%2Fjoint%2Fpscnc%2F). The 2026 Senate reform vehicle, SB 126, would add "affordability" to rate criteria rather than cap returns, per [Florida Phoenix](https://floridaphoenix.com/2025/12/09/proposal-to-reform-how-the-florida-psc-sets-energy-rates-advances-in-senate/) and the [bill analysis](https://www.flsenate.gov/Session/Bill/2026/126/Analyses/2026s00126.pre.ri.PDF). NextEra raised FPL's data center load forecast to **8 gigawatts by 2032** and its CEO said the first large load deals were "very likely" in 2026, per [Data Center Dynamics](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/nextera-raises-data-center-forecast-to-8gw-by-2032-at-florida-subsidiary-fpl/) and [T&D World](https://www.tdworld.com/utility-business/news/55353842/ceo-fpl-very-likely-to-announce-first-large-load-deals-this-year). Duke's multiyear settlement approved in August 2024 runs through 2027, per [WUSF](https://www.wusf.org/economy-business/2024-08-22/florida-commission-approves-duke-energy-settlement-increase-base-electric-rates), and the PSC approved $1.55 billion in TECO and Duke storm cost recovery, per [Fox 13](https://www.fox13news.com/news/teco-duke-looking-raise-rates-recoup-1-55b-hurricane-costs). SB 484, signed May 7, 2026, directs the PSC to "reasonably ensure" data centers pay their own costs, excludes co-ops and municipals, orders an OPPAGA study due July 1, 2027, and preserves local land use authority, per [Florida Phoenix](https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/05/07/florida-has-a-new-law-regulating-ai-data-centers/); PolitiFact rated Donalds' claim that it "ensures" rates will not rise as Half True, per [WLRN](https://www.wlrn.org/government-politics/2026-08-11/donalds-says-fl-law-will-prevent-electric-bill-hikes-from-data-centers-thats-not-guaranteed). Donalds rejected a return on equity cap in June 2026 as "a terrible solution" comparable to rent control, as documented in the first report; a Florida Politics poll found voters' blame "shifts hard" once they learn the governor picks the PSC, per [Florida Politics](https://floridapolitics.com/archives/818926-poll-voters-dont-trust-the-psc-and-blame-shifts-hard-once-they-learn-gov-desantis-picks-its-members/).

Inference. The utility and data center donors want the same thing from the PSC: approval of new gas and nuclear capacity with full cost recovery and a large load tariff hyperscalers will sign, and the only question is whether residential customers are walled off from the cost. Donalds' opposition to an ROE cap means the sole constraint on a repeat of 2025 is the Legislature's "affordability" language if it ever becomes law. Duke's expiring settlement means the next governor's PSC decides the next Duke base rates during his first term, and TECO's cycle follows. Which PSC seats expire in 2027 to 2030 was not retrievable, so the count of seats Donalds would fill is unknown.

What changes for Floridians. Electric bills keep rising on the 2025 trajectory, with FPL's 2026 to 2027 rates set unless the Supreme Court intervenes, and the cost of 8 gigawatts of data center generation is allocated by commissioners the governor appoints under a statute that says "reasonably ensure" rather than "shall not."

What Jolly would do instead. Jolly would cap regulated utility profits at the national average and impose an immediate data center moratorium, per the [ClickOrlando voters guide](https://www.clickorlando.com/voters-guide/2026/10/16/2026-voters-guide-florida-governors-race/).

Documented. Florida was its first state-level race: a $5 million pledge in February 2026 and **$3 million to American Mission Florida on March 4, 2026**, a committee chaired by Sarasota Property Appraiser Bill Furst at a Tallahassee Staples address, which bought about 1,700 spots in Tampa and Tallahassee that promoted Trump's endorsement and never mentioned AI, per [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/04/16/ai-influence-network-cash), [WUSF](https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-04-19/sarasota-property-appraiser-moving-millions-ai-moguls-support-byron-donalds) and [Hoodline](https://hoodline.com/2026/07/secretive-pro-ai-cash-fuels-byron-donalds-tv-blitz-across-florida/). The money arrived while the House sat on DeSantis' AI Bill of Rights: SB 482 passed the Senate 35 to 2 on March 6, 2026, the House gave its companion no hearing, Speaker Perez said "We do believe that the federal government should take care of AI," and after David Sacks and Taylor Budowich contacted Florida officials the House refused to take up DeSantis' April special session, per [WLRN](https://www.wlrn.org/government-politics/2026-03-06/desantis-heightens-push-for-ai-rules-as-bill-falters), [NBC News](https://nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/super-pac-backed-ai-titans-pledges-5-million-boost-byron-donalds-run-f-rcna258612) and [Florida Phoenix](https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/04/20/floridas-ai-bill-of-rights-what-happened-whats-in-it-and-whats-next/). Project Tango, a roughly 37 million square foot campus in Loxahatchee, was rejected by Palm Beach County commissioners on July 16, 2026 as "not compatible," though data center development stayed approved under prior entitlements and the county passed a moratorium, per [WLRN](https://www.wlrn.org/government-politics/2026-07-16/project-tango-ai-data-center-palm-beach-rejected) and [WFLX](https://www.wflx.com/2026/07/07/palm-beach-county-passes-ai-data-center-moratorium-project-tango-vote-is-still/). Seeking Rents counts data center interests at $30 million in Florida campaigns, per [Seeking Rents](https://jasongarcia.substack.com/p/data-center-interests-have-put-30). Donalds voted in May 2025 for the House bill with a 10-year state AI moratorium, now says he "wasn't probably the biggest fan of" it, opposes a statewide moratorium, says "If local governments don't want them, they won't build them," and introduced a federal Protecting Ratepayers Act in July 2026, per [Florida Phoenix via Orlando Weekly](https://www.orlandoweekly.com/news/florida-news/floridians-are-raising-the-alarms-over-data-centers-and-ai-where-do-byron-donalds-and-david-jolly-stand/) and [WUSF](https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-07-24/byron-donalds-opposes-statewide-moratorium-data-centers). The Anthropic-linked Public First spent more than $1 million praising Donalds for opposing federal preemption, and Alliance for Secure AI's Brendan Steinhauser said "Six months ago, he was sounding more like the industry, and now I think he sounds more like us," per [Politico via NewsBreak](https://www.newsbreak.com/politico-560779/4782517602692-the-data-center-and-ai-donors-powering-donalds-bid-for-florida-governor). A UNF poll found 68 percent of Floridians oppose a local data center and 19 local governments have paused or banned them, per Orlando Weekly. Ken Griffin, separately, called on October 21, 2026 for the country to invest in "AI, data centers, nuclear energy, batteries and robotics," per [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/10/21/ken-griffin-trump-tax-cuts-national-debt), and his $2 billion CMU Miami campus focuses on AI, national security and energy, per [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/business-leaders/ken-griffin-doubles-down-florida-record-3b-carnegie-mellon-gift).

Inference. The state hooks for a project a county rejects are the PSC's approval of generation and transmission, DEP and water management district permits, the 100 megawatt plus sales tax exemption, and any statewide preemption of local moratoria. A governor who opposes a moratorium and appoints DEP, the district boards and the PSC can clear every state gate even when a county says no, which is why Palm Beach Aggregates and Phillips money is a bet on the governor rather than the county. Donalds has become a contested figure between AI factions rather than a captured one; his record is mixed, and the most likely 2027 outcome is no state AI statute and a data center framework that stays at "reasonably ensure." The remaining $2 million of the $5 million LTF pledge was not traced.

What changes for Floridians. Siting stays local until the Legislature preempts it, water and power allocation stay with state appointees, and whether a hyperscaler's gas plant shows up on a residential bill depends on PSC enforcement of SB 484. No AI consumer protections of the kind in the dead Senate bill, such as interaction notices or a ban on AI therapy, arrive.

What Jolly would do instead. An immediate one-year moratorium with a complete ban "on the table," per [Florida Phoenix](https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/09/18/david-jolly-a-complete-ban-on-data-centers-in-florida-should-be-on-the-table/).

Donalds backs Amendment 3, promises "full and complete reform of property taxes and fees" in 2027, earlier floated a $300,000 to $400,000 homestead exemption, narrowed his fallback plan over a "math" problem, and says fiscally constrained counties should not "sing for supper," per the [ClickOrlando voters guide](https://www.clickorlando.com/voters-guide/2026/10/16/2026-voters-guide-florida-governors-race/) and [Florida Politics](https://floridapolitics.com/archives/814724-donalds-math-amendment-3/). The Taxation and Budget Reform Commission convenes every 20 years and next sits in 2027, per [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Taxation_and_Budget_Reform_Commission). House Speaker Daniel Perez, whose House authored the property tax package, led 63 members in endorsing Donalds and his committees gave $1 million, per [Florida Politics](https://floridapolitics.com/archives/754397-daniel-perez-political-committees-give-1m-boost-to-byron-donalds-campaign-for-governor/). On growth, a 2025 bill to undo county rural boundaries cleared committee and Seminole County sued, a 2026 law "makes it easier to pave over Florida farmland," and by October 13, 2026 a major developer was eyeing rural Florida with officials saying there was little they could do, per [Spectrum News 13](https://mynews13.com/fl/orlando/news/2025/08/04/county-challenges-state-bill-that-could-threaten-rural-boundary), [Florida Trident](https://floridatrib.org/2026/07/01/new-law-makes-it-easier-to-pave-over-florida-farmland/) and [WGCU](https://www.wgcu.org/government-politics/2026-10-13/major-home-developer-eyeing-rural-florida-local-officials-say-theres-little-they-can-do). Mori Hosseini remains UF trustees chair after DeSantis reappointed him June 9, 2025 amid the presidential search fight, per [WCJB](https://www.wcjb.com/2025/06/09/gov-desantis-reappoints-university-florida-trustees-amid-presidential-search-controversy/). Pat Neal and Carlos Beruff, both October donors, are suing Manatee County over impact fees, per the [Bradenton Journal](https://thebradentonjournal.substack.com/p/donations-from-neal-beruff-add-to). Airbnb's long-running ask is statewide preemption of local short-term rental rules through vehicles like SB 280, per [CBS Miami](https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/vacation-rental-proposal-on-the-move-in-senate); whether DeSantis vetoed the 2024 version could not be confirmed.

Inference. The Realtors' return is transactional: a bigger exemption raises what buyers can pay, which raises prices and commissions, and the benefit concentrates in higher value homesteads while renters, commercial owners and non-homestead owners face the backfill. The developers' asks are executive as much as legislative: DEP and the five water management district boards issue wetlands and water permits, the governor appoints the Commerce secretary who reviews plan amendments and the Florida Housing board that allocates Live Local money, and he signs impact fee and sprawl bills. Perez's $1 million is leadership buying a governor who signs the House agenda DeSantis slow-walked, and the 63 House endorsements set up a 2027 session where the House and governor are aligned against the Senate. Donalds' "sing for supper" line implies state backfill for rural counties, which is a statement of intent, not a costed plan.

What changes for Floridians. Homestead owners see a lower bill in 2027 and a lower one in 2028; everyone else sees higher millage on non-homestead property, new fees, or thinner fire, EMS, library and park budgets, with the sheriffs split by whether their county has commercial tax base to absorb the shift. Rural boundaries and farmland get easier to convert, and local short-term rental rules may be preempted.

What Jolly would do instead. Jolly opposes Amendment 3 and would "restore home rule over property taxes" and fully fund Sadowski housing money, per the ClickOrlando guide.

## Insurance and tort: a plan that changes nothing carriers won

Documented. Citizens has shrunk to about 270,000 policies through depopulation and a non-renewal push while S&P projects its largest full year underwriting loss, per [Insurance Business](https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/property/citizens-cuts-policy-count-to-270000-amid-nonrenewal-push-588731.aspx) and [S&P Global](https://spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/rapidly-shrinking-citizens-property-projects-largest-full-year-underwriting-loss). His "$1,000 hurricane tax" label for Jolly's plan relies on an FSU study that did not examine Jolly's proposal and would apply only after a catastrophic storm, per [WUFT](https://www.wuft.org/politics/2026-10-16/fact-checking-claims-from-florida-governor-candidates-david-jolly-and-byron-donalds) and [PolitiFact](https://politifact.com/article/2026/sep/21/jolly-donalds-hurricane-insurance-1000-florida/). The James Madison Institute argues for restoring Citizens to insurer of last resort, per [JMI](https://jamesmadison.org/from-backstop-to-market-participant-reassessing-citizens-role-restoring-citizens-property-insurance-corporation-to-its-role-as-floridas-insurer-of-last-resort/). The direct insurance money in the file is small, Heritage P&C's $50,000 and Kompothecras' $79,000, as the first report documented.

Inference. The industry's 2027 ask is defensive: keep tort reform, keep Citizens' eligibility tightening, and secure state reinsurance support. The gainers are carriers and reinsurers; the losers are policyholders pushed off Citizens into higher takeout offers. The small visible insurance money suggests either giving through trade committees the notes could not trace or that the alignment did not need to be bought.

What changes for Floridians. Homeowners keep leaving Citizens for private carriers at higher premiums, the one-way attorney fee and assignment of benefits limits stay, and the Cat Fund surcharge on every policy falls if reserves hold, which is relief that evaporates after the next big storm.

What Jolly would do instead. A state catastrophe wind fund removing hurricane coverage from the private market, whose 60 to 70 percent savings claim fact checkers judged unlikely, per WUFT.

John Snyder's Educator Solutions was paid $6.93 million by Optima-run charters in 2020 to 2022 and paid Erika more than $500,000, per [Florida Bulldog](https://www.floridabulldog.org/2025/06/firms-belonging-to-rep-donalds-wife-grabbed-millions-in-charter-school-contracts/). No source links either man to Tikvah, Shalem, Im Tirtzu or Regavim. ## Conclusion

The second hop changes the picture in one important way: the blocs are not independent. The attorney general, who shares the Seminole Tribe, GEO, CDR and Kalshi as donors with the governor, decides whether Florida sues prediction markets, defends the compact and enforces any AI statute; the PSC that sets utility returns also decides who pays for the data centers the AI investors want built; the emergency fund that pays detention vendors is the same fund that pays for hurricanes; and the House Speaker whose committees gave $1 million wrote the property tax amendment the Realtors are spending $18 million to pass. A Donalds administration would therefore be less a series of favors to donors than a single governing coalition, Perez's House plus Uthmeier's office plus a Koch-trained executive staff, that has already set its 2027 agenda: Amendment 3 implementation and a follow-on cut, no ROE cap, no data center moratorium, no voucher controls, continued detention funding, and silence on the compact until a court forces the question.

The decision that will reveal the most is the one he has refused to discuss. Every other bloc got a stated position before Election Day. On gambling he took $5.5 million from the Tribe and more than $1 million from the prediction markets and sportsbooks suing or being sued by it, and said nothing. Whether his first FGCC appointment, his first amicus decision after the Supreme Court acts, and his response to the Broward case favor the Tribe or the exchanges will show whether the money bought access or bought an outcome, and it is a decision with a nine-figure annual revenue line attached to it.

# PART 4: RAW RESEARCH NOTES

Ten researcher note files. Each has a takeaway, cited findings with URLs, inferences, and gaps. Treat gaps sections as the verification to-do list.

### Note: federal_money_and_pacs.md

_Folder: Byron Donalds money and donor network_

### Byron Donalds: Federal Campaign Finance History and PAC Network (2020 through Oct 2026)

Scope note: This file covers the federal layer (Byron Donalds for Congress, his leadership PACs, joint fundraising committees, outside spending in FL-19 races, FEC enforcement). Where state committee figures (Friends of Byron Donalds PAC, the governor race) surfaced in the same sources, they are recorded in a separate section at the end so the tracker can be loaded, but a separate researcher owns that layer.

Access note: OpenSecrets pages were blocked by the fetch tool and the FEC API was blocked by the proxy, so cycle totals come from FEC.gov committee and candidate pages and ProPublica FEC Itemizer. Industry breakdowns per cycle from OpenSecrets could not be retrieved and are listed as a gap.

#### Committee map (FEC IDs, treasurer, registration dates)

##### Takeaway
Every federal Donalds committee is run by treasurer Bradley T. Crate of Red Curve Solutions, Beverly, MA. He controls one principal campaign committee, two leadership PACs (a second one registered December 2024), and one joint fundraising committee whose participants include the NRCC and the Republican Party of Florida.

##### Cited Findings
- Byron Donalds for Congress, FEC ID C00733329, principal campaign committee for candidate H2FL14186; Donalds filed his Statement of Candidacy for FL-19 on January 6, 2020, [FEC candidate page](https://www.fec.gov/data/candidate/H2FL14186/); [MUR 7783 First General Counsel's Report](https://www.fec.gov/files/legal/murs/7783/7783_13.pdf)
- Treasurer of Byron Donalds for Congress: Bradley T. Crate, [ProPublica Itemizer, 2024 cycle](https://projects.propublica.org/itemizer/committee/C00733329/2024); [FEC MUR 7783 page](https://www.fec.gov/data/legal/matter-under-review/7783/)
- Proven Conservatives PAC, FEC ID C00755728, designated Leadership PAC, registered August 20, 2020, listed by ProPublica as "LEADERSHIP PAC - DONALDS, BYRON", treasurer Bradley T. Crate, [FEC committee page](https://www.fec.gov/data/committee/C00755728/); [ProPublica Itemizer 2022](https://projects.propublica.org/itemizer/committee/C00755728/2022)
- Proven Conservatives PAC - Federal, FEC ID C00894147, labeled Leadership PAC, Quarterly PAC Qualified, registered December 19, 2024, [FEC committee page](https://www.fec.gov/data/committee/C00894147/)
- Byron Donalds Victory Fund, FEC ID C00760108, joint fundraising committee, original Form 1 filed October 1, 2020; amended Form 1 filed December 19, 2024 and again March 23, 2026; treasurer and custodian of records Bradley T. Crate, c/o Red Curve Solutions, 100 Cummings Center Ste 306-P, Beverly MA 01915, [FEC committee page](https://www.fec.gov/data/committee/C00760108/); [FEC filings list](https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-bin/forms/C00760108/); [Form 1, March 23, 2026](https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-bin/forms/C00760108/1955929/)
- Byron Donalds Victory Fund participants per the Dec 19, 2024 and Mar 23, 2026 Form 1s: (1) Byron Donalds for Congress C00733329, (2) Proven Conservatives PAC C00755728, (3) Republican Party of Florida C00099259, (4) NRCC C00075820, (5) Proven Conservatives PAC - Federal C00894147, [Form 1 Dec 2024](https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-bin/forms/C00760108/1860265/); [Form 1 Mar 2026](https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-bin/forms/C00760108/1955929/)
- Mooney-Donalds JFC, FEC ID C00819615, joint fundraising committee with Rep. Alex Mooney, registered July 1, 2022, status Terminated; raised $39,445 (coverage July 1 to Oct 19, 2022), $38,945 from individuals, $500 from other committees; transferred $37,693.12 to participating committees and spent $1,751.88 on operations; ended with $0, [FEC committee page](https://www.fec.gov/data/committee/C00819615/)
- Byron Donalds Victory Fund donation page exists on WinRed, [WinRed](https://secure.winred.com/byron-donalds-victory-fund/socal)

##### Inferences
- The "Proven Conservatives PAC - Federal" committee created Dec 2024 is likely a second leadership PAC vehicle set up alongside the governor run; FEC labels it a leadership PAC with $0 independent expenditures, so it is not a super PAC.
- Because the Victory Fund's participants include the NRCC and RPOF, large checks to the Victory Fund can be split across party committees at higher limits.

##### Gaps
- The Form 1 allocation formula for the Victory Fund was not extracted.
- Who funds Proven Conservatives PAC - Federal (only $15,000 in individual contributions through Sept 30, 2026) was not itemized.

#### Byron Donalds for Congress: cycle totals 2020 through 2026

##### Takeaway
Donalds raised about $3.25M (2020), $5.66M (2022), $6.60M (2024) and only $738K through mid 2026 for his House committee, which has spent heavily in 2025 and 2026 (including a $1.2M transfer to his state governor PAC) while raising little.

##### Cited Findings
- 2019-2020 cycle (coverage Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2020): total receipts $3,250,540.96; individual contributions $2,915,688.05 (itemized $1,816,900.47, unitemized $1,098,787.58); other committee (PAC) contributions $320,250.00; candidate loans $0; transfers in from other authorized committees $8,219.17; disbursements $2,769,646.89; ending cash $480,894.07, [FEC committee page, 2020](https://www.fec.gov/data/committee/C00733329/?cycle=2020)
- 2020 race context: GOP primary rival Casey Askar raised $7,253,992 (largely self funded per campaignmoney.com listing of $3.5M raised) and spent $7,259,535; Democrat Cindy Banyai raised $214,750, [ProPublica race page 2020](https://projects.propublica.org/itemizer/races/2020/states/fl/house/19)
- 2021-2022 cycle: total receipts $5,657,617.12; individual contributions $4,621,136.22; other committee contributions $571,750.00; disbursements $5,400,519.91; ending cash $737,991.28, [FEC candidate page, 2022](https://www.fec.gov/data/candidate/H2FL14186/?cycle=2022&election_full=true)
- 2023-2024 cycle: total receipts $6,600,931.63; individual contributions $4,812,440.63; other committee contributions $682,634.15; disbursements $5,598,912.45; ending cash $1,740,010.46, [FEC candidate page, 2024](https://www.fec.gov/data/candidate/H2FL14186/?cycle=2024&election_full=true)
- 2024 cycle detail: between Aug 4 and Nov 2, 2024 the committee filed 22 "48 Hour Notice" reports ranging $1,000 to $19,200 (largest filed Oct 31, 2024, $19,200); 2024 year end report showed $5,258.14 in debts, [ProPublica Itemizer 2024](https://projects.propublica.org/itemizer/committee/C00733329/2024)
- 2025-2026 cycle (coverage Jan 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026): total receipts $738,092.00; individual contributions $533,501.80; other committee contributions $56,800.00; disbursements $2,143,626.16; ending cash $334,476.30, [FEC candidate page](https://www.fec.gov/data/candidate/H2FL14186/)
- 2026 cycle per FundVoter (through Sept 30, 2026 reports): raised $738,092; individuals $533,502 (72%); transfers, loans and other $147,790 (20%); PACs $56,800 (8%); total spent $2,240,519; fundraising costs $164,521; mail and print $279,675; median active House incumbent raised $1,743,643 so Donalds is at about 0.4x median, [FundVoter](https://fundvoter.org/politicians/byron-donalds)
- Recent 2026 PAC receipts named by FundVoter: Rising Phoenix PAC $7,000 (July 23, 2026); CGCN PAC three contributions totaling $5,000 (May 27, 2026); Sysco $2,500 (Apr 29, 2026); Friends of Neal Dunn $1,000 (Feb 3, 2026); lobbyist contributions $113,800 across 38 entries including June 4, 17 and 18, 2026, [FundVoter](https://fundvoter.org/politicians/byron-donalds)
- FundVoter 2026 cycle industry tally (its "Trace the Influence" tool, only 5 of 11 industries shown): Finance/Banking $112K; Oil and Gas/Energy $51.5K; Real Estate $20K; Agriculture $18.5K; Tech $12K, [FundVoter](https://fundvoter.org/politicians/byron-donalds)
- FundVoter top 2026 PAC organizations: American Council of Engineering Companies PAC $15,000 (4 contributions); State Farm Federal PAC $14,000 (8); NextEra Energy PAC $12,000 (5), [FundVoter](https://fundvoter.org/politicians/byron-donalds)
- Donalds' House campaign transferred $1.2 million to the state committee Friends of Byron Donalds within two days of his Feb 25, 2025 governor announcement, [Florida Trident, Sept 8, 2025](https://floridatrident.org/byron-donalds-skirts-campaign-finance-laws/); [Florida Bulldog, Aug 24, 2025](https://www.floridabulldog.org/2025/08/the-two-campaigns-byron-donalds-he-appears-violating-state-law/)

##### Inferences
- The 2026 cycle disbursements ($2.14M) exceed receipts ($738K) by about $1.4M, consistent with the $1.2M transfer to the state PAC plus wind down spending from the $1.74M cash on hand at end of 2024.
- The FundVoter page's AIPAC figure ($59,864) exceeds its total 2026 PAC receipts ($56,800), so that AIPAC number is an all-cycle figure, not a 2026 one.

##### Gaps
- OpenSecrets per-cycle industry and top contributor tables (securities, real estate, insurance, oil and gas, health, crypto) could not be fetched (site blocked). The 2020 PAC list from Paradise Progressive (below) and FundVoter's 2026 partial tally are the only industry-type breakdowns obtained.

- Florida law issue: Fla. Stat. bars qualifying for more than one office with overlapping terms; Donalds filed FEC paperwork for re-election in Nov 2024 and state paperwork for governor in Feb 2025; Crate formed the state PAC Friends of Byron Donalds on Feb 26, 2025; experts (Ian Vandewalker, Brennan Center; Jeff Swartz, Cooley Law) said he may violate the spirit but not the letter and that FEC enforcement is unlikely, [Florida Bulldog](https://www.floridabulldog.org/2025/08/the-two-campaigns-byron-donalds-he-appears-violating-state-law/); [Florida Trident](https://floridatrident.org/byron-donalds-skirts-campaign-finance-laws/)
- Campaign payments to Larry Wilcoxson and Wilcoxson Consulting from Byron Donalds for Congress: $133,450 across 160+ disbursements July 7, 2020 to March 24, 2025, including payroll $75,250, payroll taxes $18,750, consulting $22,500, travel $8,450; more than $86,000 after May 2024, [The Blaze opinion column, May 30, 2025](https://www.theblaze.com/columns/opinion/byron-donalds-pays-body-man-with-a-rap-sheet-using-campaign-cash) (opinion piece using FEC data; the Farley Substack separately claims $419,000 to Wilcoxson citing OpenSecrets, unverified)

##### Inferences
- The 2020 chain (state PAC to CFEG to state PAC to federal super PAC) and the 2025 federal-to-state $1.2M transfer are the two episodes most likely to be cited by opponents as pattern evidence of moving money across the federal/state line.

##### Gaps
- No OCE or House Ethics complaint about Donalds' campaign finances was found.
- Whether any of the ~$400,000 was later refunded (post Aug 2025 filings) was not verified.

##### Takeaway
The main outside vehicle is American Mission Florida, a state PC chaired by Sarasota Property Appraiser Bill Furst and funded entirely by the AI-industry federal super PAC Leading the Future ($3M on Mar. 4, 2026; $5M pledged); Club for Growth Action Florida routed Yass money; AFP Action and Florida Chamber endorsed without disclosed spending. Against Donalds, Conservatives for Ethical Leadership (Lincoln Project-affiliated, funded by Affordable Florida) and the DGA ($1M for Jolly, Oct. 20, 2026) are the only reported spenders.

##### Cited Findings
- Leading the Future (federal super PAC, FEC C00916114; Andreessen Horowitz $25M, Marc Andreessen $12.5M, Ben Horowitz $12.5M, Greg and Anna Brockman $25M) pledged $5M to boost Donalds; gave American Mission Florida $3M on Mar. 4, 2026; American Mission Florida put about $2M into pro-Donalds ads by April; registered with the state in February 2026 listing a Tallahassee Staples store as address; chaired by Bill Furst, [WGCU, Apr. 17, 2026](https://news.wgcu.org/text/top-story/2026-04-17/sarasotas-property-appraiser-is-moving-millions-from-ai-moguls-to-support-byron-donalds); [NBC News](https://nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/super-pac-backed-ai-titans-pledges-5-million-boost-byron-donalds-run-f-rcna258612)

- Democratic Governors Association announced $1,000,000 for Jolly on Oct. 20, 2026 (spokesperson Kevin Donohoe), [Florida Phoenix, Oct. 20, 2026](https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/10/20/democratic-governors-association-investing-1-million-to-support-david-jolly/)
- Pro-Collins (primary): Florida Fighters (political nonprofit, donors undisclosed) funded nearly $1.1M in TV ads on Collins' Green Beret service (mid-2025), [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/ron-desantis-lobbying-megadonor-ken-griffin-stays-sidelines-florida-go-rcna244801)
- Historical: 2020 FEC MUR 7783 (CLC complaint) alleged Friends of Byron Donalds (then treasurer Noreen Fenner) and Conservatives for Effective Government (treasurer David Ramba) moved soft money to a super PAC backing his House run; FEC deadlocked 3-3 and closed file 6-0, "Dismissed-Other", [FEC MUR 7783](https://www.fec.gov/data/legal/matter-under-review/7783/)

#### Key Question 3: Kohelet Policy Forum, Yass and Dantchik

##### Takeaway
Kohelet (founded January 2012 by Moshe Koppel) produced the policy papers underpinning the 2023 judicial overhaul pushed by Yariv Levin and Simcha Rothman. Haaretz (March 2021) named both Yass and Arthur Dantchik as Kohelet's principal funders through opaque US vehicles, but later reporting (NYT, Washington Post, Calcalist, JTA) says Yass never donated and Dantchik was the dominant donor (Calcalist: ~93% of budget). Dantchik announced on August 4, 2023 that he had stopped funding Israeli think tanks including Kohelet; Kohelet cut roughly half its staff in April 2024 and its donations fell from 30M shekels (2022) to 13.6M shekels (2024).

##### Cited Findings
What Kohelet is
- Established January 2012 by Moshe Koppel (chair), run with Avraham Diskin, Avi Bell and Eugene Kontorovich. Says it takes only private donations. Largest donations are anonymous, several million dollars, routed through the American nonprofit American Friends of Kohelet Policy Forum (Haaretz, Oct 5, 2018)., [Wikipedia: Kohelet Policy Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kohelet_Policy_Forum)

#### Key question 4: What Donalds has promised, and what the governor controls

##### Takeaway
Donalds has promised to remove local officials and state attorneys who adopt "sanctuary" policies and says Florida will "never" be a sanctuary state, and he frames enforcement as a nonnegotiable federal mandate; the governor controls FDEM (which runs the detention sites and emergency no bid procurement under a state of emergency the governor can keep extending), sits on and chairs the unanimous vote State Board of Immigration Enforcement that controls $250M in local grants and detention bed strategy, and under SB 2-C can suspend officials who do not comply.

##### Cited Findings
- Aug 2026, after a Tampa rally: Donalds said Florida is not and will never be a sanctuary state; local officials who create sanctuaries will be removed; state attorneys who do not enforce the law "are going to be removed from office, because it destabilizes law and order"; he would not hesitate to suspend them, [Florida Phoenix (Mitch Perry), Aug 12, 2026](https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/08/12/byron-donalds-says-hell-remove-local-officials-who-indulge-in-sanctuary-policies/)
- Oct 13, 2026 Jacksonville business roundtable: Donalds said a governor must follow federal law, "States don't set immigration policy. The federal government does," rejected the idea governors choose how enforcement is carried out, and was unsympathetic to a homebuilder's complaint about ICE worksite raids, [Florida Phoenix, Oct 14, 2026](https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/10/14/byron-donalds-says-states-must-work-with-ice-but-a-dozen-of-them-arent/)

- FDEM projects $500M for Operation Vigilant Sentry in FY 2026-27, [WUSF, Sept 17, 2026](https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-09-17/fdem-spent-about-1-billion-immigration-last-year-now-itll-get-more)
- Kevin Guthrie (then FDEM director) on why the state could build so fast: "We understand how to act fast without bureaucracy in the face of any emergency", [NBC Miami/AP, July 3, 2025](https://www.nbcmiami.com/news/local/republican-donors-and-floridas-hurricane-know-how-helped-build-alligator-alcatraz-so-quickly/3651580/)

##### Inferences
- The specific levers a Governor Donalds would hold: (1) whether to keep extending the Jan 2023 immigration emergency, which is the legal basis for FDEM's no bid purchase orders; (2) who runs FDEM and thus which vendors get paid first from the $417M backlog and the $187M just appropriated; (3) whether to renew or expand GEO|CDR Baker at Deportation Depot or reopen a third site; (4) the Board of Immigration Enforcement's $250M grant program and detention bed strategy; (5) the FY 2027-28 budget request for Operation Vigilant Sentry; (6) suspension power over noncompliant local officials.
